scope: Model resolution, model identity, weight loading, dtype, quantization semantics and runtime memory parameters.

claims.claim: vLLM resolves Hugging Face compatible models by inspecting the architectures field in config.json and matching a registered model implementation.
claims.notes: hf_overrides can correct an architecture label but cannot add an unsupported implementation.

claims.claim: Model revision, tokenizer revision and code revision are separate configuration identities and may need independent pinning.
claims.notes: Tokenizer follows model revision by default only when both refer to the same repository.

claims.claim: trust_remote_code defaults to false; enabling it is a decision to trust and execute remote model or tokenizer code.
claims.notes: Do not enable it as a generic compatibility workaround.

claims.claim: Current ModelConfig dtype=auto maps FP32 and FP16 model configs to FP16 and BF16 configs to BF16.
claims.notes: Hardware and model constraints still apply.

claims.claim: vLLM quantization docs distinguish method (checkpoint loading implementation), scheme (tensor numeric format and scales), and kernel (execution implementation).
claims.notes: W4A16 describes 4-bit weights and 16-bit activations; it does not mean total model memory is exactly one quarter.

claims.claim: max_model_len limits the full sequence context including prompt and output; -1 or auto requests automatic selection constrained by available GPU memory.
claims.notes: Model-declared context capability and cache capacity still constrain the result.

claims.claim: Current CacheConfig documents conditional gpu_memory_utilization defaults: 1.0 with extensible KV cache and 0.92 otherwise; kv_cache_memory_bytes overrides the automatic KV cache budget.
claims.notes: Commit-specific behavior; do not generalize to older releases or unsupported platforms.

claims.claim: The default model loader reads checkpoint weights through weight iterators and loads them into an initialized model before post-load processing.
claims.notes: Checkpoint formats and optimized paths vary by model and release.
